**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 00:58
- [USER] User inquired about exceptions for the importation of electronic waste for proper treatment and disposal.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant confirmed the ability to provide more information regarding the importation of electronic waste for proper treatment and disposal.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In Indonesia, the importation of electronic waste is regulated by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Ministry of Environment and Forestry is responsible for issuing permits and overseeing the proper management of electronic waste.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Specific regulations outline the conditions under which electronic waste can be imported, including the requirement for proper treatment and disposal facilities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Environmentally sound management practices are required for the importation of electronic waste.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Indonesian Government Regulation No. 101/2014 on the Management of Electronic Waste outlines the procedures for the importation and management of electronic waste in the country.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Regulation No. 101/2014 requires that electronic waste imported for treatment and disposal must be processed in accordance with Indonesian environmental regulations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Imported electronic waste must not pose a threat to human health and the environment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] International agreements, such as the Basel Convention, regulate the importation of electronic waste.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Basel Convention requires that electronic waste be managed in an environmentally sound manner.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Basel Convention stipulates that electronic waste must not be exported from developed countries to developing countries without the consent of the receiving country.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant expressed hope that the information provided was helpful and invited the user to ask for more information or references if needed.
